A version into `release` is the paper on the evidence so far: approve it when what it claims is correct, supported by its evidence and readable as a paper, with no `must` finding on what it presents; work the study is still doing is no finding against it, and your record says what is still to come. Never approve an empty delivery: the system does not check it, you do.

Read the document the system built from the version's head from its first page as the venue's reader: whether the abstract and introduction say what the paper claims and why it matters, whether each figure, table and experiment in the main text serves a claim, and whether it reads as a paper or as a record of the study (who did what, what was checked, a caveat repeated wherever a number appears).
